register: The PostgreSQL build the engine runs from
note: QGD-ENG-0004. One pinned build, verified by SHA-256 before it is used. The machine's own PostgreSQL is never used — on a developer's Mac there is usually one on PATH, and an engine that silently ran against it would be a different database from the one that ships. scripts/fetch-postgres.mjs downloads and verifies this; src/engine/binaries.ts refuses anything whose hash does not match.

source.what: Zonky's embedded-postgres binaries, on Maven Central. The only PostgreSQL build published for macOS arm64: EDB publishes osx-binaries for x86-64 and returns 403 for arm64.

presentButUnused.why: pg_ctl builds the postmaster command line as a string and runs it through a shell, which is the one place a shell survived in this code path and what QGD-SEC-0002 bans everywhere we write ourselves. The supervisor already owns the lifecycle, so it spawns postgres directly with an argument array. The program is in the build; nothing uses it.

absent.why: QGD-ENG-0005. This build carries the server and its two lifecycle tools and nothing else. Backup is therefore a copy of the stopped data directory (QGD-ENG-0011), not a dump.

trim.note: QGD-ENG-0004.1. The published build is 356 MB; almost half of it is the same file stored under two or three names, and most of the rest is machinery this product never reaches. scripts/trim-postgres.mjs applies this after the download has been verified against the SHA-256 above, so the trim is only ever applied to a tree already known to be genuine.

plugins.why: plpgsql because initdb installs it into template1 and will not finish without it; pgoutput because it is core rather than contrib; dict_snowball because initdb runs snowball_create.sql, and CREATE FUNCTION checks that the library it names is there. Everything else in lib/postgresql is a procedural language, a contrib module, or a conversion between character encodings this product never uses — the database is UTF8 and so is the only client that connects to it. An allow list rather than a deny list: a later version that added a module would otherwise ship it without anyone deciding to.

extensions.why: The control and script files for the one extension that is kept. initdb reads these; the rest describe contrib modules that are no longer here.

keptBecauseInitdbReadsThem.why: initdb reads all of share/postgresql and refuses to finish if a piece of it is missing: snowball_create.sql builds the text-search dictionaries in template1, those dictionaries name stopword files in tsearch_data, and sql_features.txt fills in information_schema. Tried removing each; initdb named them one at a time. Together they are under a megabyte and a half, so nothing in share is removed at all — the sample files beside them are not worth a separate decision.
